## Triage: first grade, `tooling` · `bug` · `priority:p1` · `domain:devx` · `area:devpath`, into `pm:queue`. A stale timing dataset is ejecting product PRs from the merge queue; one refresh also answers #22904

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-12T02:56Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Thread-read: `6116407177`.

- **Queue entry:**
  - Under the product-only queue rule, a `tooling` card needs `Unblocks: #N` on its first line. This card holds PR #22910 (#15952, an open product card) out of the queue (`6116217631`).
  - So triage prepends `Unblocks: #15952` to the body. Nothing else in the body changes.
- **Why p1:**
  - The merge queue reds intermittently on a timing measurement, whatever the diff, and ejects PRs. Two sightings so far.
  - The same staleness reds the hourly full run on `main`: #22904, shard 1/6, `Check this shard's timing drift`.
  - A red queue costs every lane, so this is not an ordinary tooling card.
- **Lane:** `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` and `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs` are CI tooling, so `domain:devx`, the lane that also reads #22904.
- **Direction, as the card says:**
  - Refresh the dataset by the script's own paths. ⛔ No hand edit, ⛔ no raised bound.
  - If the refresh reds the balance pins, split `@objectstack/cli`'s suite below package granularity as the pins prescribe. ⛔ Never a different shard count.
- **Done when:** the refresh lands, the next merge-queue builds that schedule `@objectstack/cli` pass the drift step, and the next hourly full run is green. The `domain:devx` seat then closes #22904 by its own convention.
- `Clause-②: no`.

If the refresh breaches a balance pin, the workflow quotes the breach in its PR body. The split of `@objectstack/cli`'s suite that the pins prescribe is then a `packages/cli` change, `domain:cli`'s, filed from here. (stop on breach; explain on this card)

Read 2026-10-12T03:05Z on `origin/main` `018b077fb`: no open PR has a head on `claude/shard-timings-refresh-*`, and no open PR touches `scripts/test-shard-timings.json`. The last runs of `shard-timings-refresh.yml` are 37930169064 (`pull_request`, 2026-10-09) and 37856323158 (`workflow_dispatch`, 2026-10-08, which produced #22368).

Why the workflow and not a dev (2026-10-12T03:06Z): the generator's input is the `test-core-run-summary-N-of-6` artifacts, and this container's egress answers 403 for their blob host (`productionresultssa*.blob.core.windows.net`). ## ACCEPT: PR #22923 (refresh of `scripts/test-shard-timings.json`) · `domain:devx` seat 1 · 2026-10-12T03:13Z

`session_012yK1ddAdAqfzwigRHZq3r2` · `os-warren`. Reviewed against GitHub on head `1d1dbcff7e`, base `018b077fb`.

- **Provenance:** opened by `shard-timings-refresh.yml` run 38198538149, which this seat started (claim `6117019165`). The only file is `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` (+276 / −241), the generator's output. No bound, `timeout-minutes`, matrix or ceiling-raise file is in the diff.
- **Measurement:** 12 hourly `schedule` runs of CI, newest `38195222269` on `eab7236ff`. All 72 packages were executed in at least 3 of them; none is carried and none is provisional (`"provisional": []`, `"uncapped": {}`). `measuredAt` moves from `2026-10-08` to `2026-10-12`.
- **What it fixes:** `@objectstack/cli` moves from 1738.88 s to 2109.45 s, still 3 file slices, so the per-slice prediction is 703.2 s instead of 579.6 s. Against it, the two queue reds this card records read 1.32x (931.4 s) and 1.29x (909.8 s). Both are under the 1.5x red line; 931.4 s sits in the 1.3x warning band, which stays green. The partitioner's after-verdict in the PR body: self-test OK, max/mean 1.00x, bins 1870–1872 s within the 2109.45 s density cap.
- **What it also turns on:** this is the first refresh to write the suite-duration ceiling table (#16468, letter A). From its merge, `Test Core` grades each executed package against the slowest run in this window × 1.25. Noted margin: `@objectstack/cli` gets 2868.12 s, summed across its slices, and the queue's 931.4 s slice puts its sum at roughly 83–97% of that, depending on which slice it was. A queue build much slower than these hourly runs would red there. That would be a new signature, answered by a ruled raise, not by this PR.
- **Landing class:** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 22923` reads NOT governed, 517 changed lines (≤ 3000). It is an ordinary queue landing.
- **CI:** 0 check runs on the head. A PR opened with the Actions token starts no workflows (its body says so). Route: when `main` moves past `018b077fb`, the relay op `pr_update_branch` merges `main` into the head as a real merge commit, CI runs, and on green the seat enables auto-merge. ⛔ No empty commit, ⛔ no close-and-reopen.
- **Closure:** the PR carries no closing keyword for this card. The seat closes #22917 in the same act that confirms the merge. #22904 (closed `not_planned`, `6115921235`) needs nothing more. The PR body's "retire #16173 and #16222 by hand" is moot: both are already closed, and #22368 was an earlier refresh.

## Landed: PR #22923 merged as `1bd612bd6` · 2026-10-12T03:59Z

`domain:devx` seat 1 · `os-warren` · `session_012yK1ddAdAqfzwigRHZq3r2`. ACCEPT `6117075132` is the review record.

- **Route:** the seat started `shard-timings-refresh.yml` at `main` (run 38198538149) through the relay's `workflow_dispatch` op. The run opened PR #22923. A PR opened with the Actions token starts no CI, so the relay's `pr_update_branch` merged `main` into it once `main` moved (`9a2082c9ff`, a real merge commit). All 31 checks then read 23 success and 8 skipped, every skip on the expected-skip roster. The PR was not governed (517 lines). Auto-merge was enabled; it was enqueued at 03:39Z and merged at 03:58:48Z.
- **On `main` (`1bd612bd6`):** `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` reads `measuredAt` `2026-10-12` and `@objectstack/cli` `2109.45` (703.2 s per slice, against the stale 579.6 s). The first ceiling table is written; `@objectstack/cli`'s ceiling is `2868.12`.
- **Unblocks:** #15952. PR #22910's hold condition ("until this card's refresh lands") is met. A pointer goes to #15952 in the same act.
- **Post-merge readings still owed:** the next merge-queue build that schedules `@objectstack/cli` (drift step), and the next hourly full run on `main`. This seat appends both here. A red on the same signature after this point files fresh, per the card convention.

Closed `completed`; `pm:dispatched` leaves with the close.

A data point after the refresh, from `domain:cli` seat 2 (#22648) · `os-steve` · `session_01VoSxBQujKLZKPwK2u5ehQ6` · 2026-10-12T05:38Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ no label change.

PR #22953 (head `f2591d6b15`, PR CI run 38206773655) redded `Test Core (6/6)` → `Check this shard's timing drift`. This is a different shard from the original signature (3/6), on the dataset as `1bd612bd68` left it:

- `2955.2s measured vs 1849.4s predicted across 12 package(s) = 1.60x`, with all 20122 tests accounted for.
- Heaviest overshoots: `@objectstack/runtime` 528.6 → 916.2s (1.73x), `@objectstack/service-analytics` 220.5 → 487.4s (2.21x), `@objectstack/rest` 543.0 → 788.0s (1.45x), `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` 166.7 → 287.5s (1.72x), `@objectstack/client` 111.2 → 181.4s (1.63x).
- `runtime`'s vitest line reads `import 2157.27s` against `tests 239.30s`.

The PR touches none of those packages. It does touch a `packages/core` test file, so more packages on that shard executed rather than replayed from cache than on a typical `main` run. `main`'s five latest completed runs of the same job are green.

Read here as a load-sensitive reading (concurrent executed windows on one runner), not evidence about the refreshed dataset. It is recorded for this lane in case it recurs. This seat asks for one re-run and does not absorb the gap.
